question: P, Q and R invest sum in the ratio of 2 : 22 : 70, respectively. If they earned a total profit of ₹4,700 at the end of the year, then what is the difference between share of Q and R?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Profit** = Ratio of **Investment** = 2 : 22 : 70.

Total ratio parts = 2 + 22 + 70 = 94 units.

94 units = ₹4,700 ⇒ 1 unit = 4700 ÷ 94 = ₹50.

Difference between **Q and R** = 70 − 22 = 48 units.

Difference in profit = 48 × 50 = ₹2,400.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Investment Ratio (P:Q:R) = 2:22:70 | Total Profit = ₹4,700.
Formulas: Profit Share = (Individual Ratio ÷ Total Ratio) × Total Profit | Difference = ProfitR − ProfitQ.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9331f799e2def072a33a3f8d02cb95037a46591ffcf182ab2ffee83824f4506e.png] 
⇒ Sum of ratios = 2 + 22 + 70 = 94.
⇒ Profit of Q = (22 ÷ 94) × 4700 = 22 × 50 = ₹1,100.
⇒ Profit of R = (70 ÷ 94) × 4700 = 70 × 50 = ₹3,500.
⇒ Difference = 3500 − 1100 = ₹2,400.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Principle

When the **time period** of investment is the same for all partners, the profit is distributed directly in the ratio of their **capital investments**.

Variable Time Investment

If time periods differ, Profit Ratio = (Capital₁ × Time₁) : (Capital₂ × Time₂).
